subject: Post-demo: PetraHealth model fit, eval pack, and pin/rollback options
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@petrahealth.com>, PetraHealth IT <it-account-team@petrahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: PetraHealth model fit, eval pack, and pin/rollback options

Emma / PetraHealth IT — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a short trial: 

Recap:
- Use case: patient triage summarization + guideline-aware followups for clinical ops.
- Key constraints: high factuality on guideline references, <200ms p50 latency target for single-turn summarization, and strict PII handling.

What we’re attaching for your team:
- eval pack (petra_eval_pack_v1.zip): curated prompt set (18 prompts) + synthetic and redacted real snippets representative of your traffic.
- prompt set CSV (petra_prompt_set_v1.csv) with expected outputs and grade rubric.

Recommended model variants to start with for your workload (based on our bench & your prompt set):
1) redwood-1.6-stable — conservative weights, best-known factuality profile (recommended for initial trial & for pinning).
2) redwood-1.7-qa — slightly higher throughput; may be useful for less-critical summarization paths.

Important note (transparency): we rolled a platform model update (redwood-2.0 rollout) earlier this month. For most customers it improved latency and throughput, but on a small subset of clinical-style prompts we observed a regressed factuality signal.
- Recommendation: Pin trial traffic to redwood-1.6-stable while you run the eval pack. That will give you a stable baseline and avoid surprises from ongoing platform rollouts.

Next steps proposed: 
1) We’ll share the eval pack (attached). Please run the rubric against a representative sample (we can help grade).
2) Redwood will provision a 2-week trial with pinning to redwood-1.6-stable for your account (to be confirmed).
3) If you see issues in the eval, we’ll provide diffs and an action plan (pin+patch or targeted rollback).

Could you confirm: preferred start date for the trial, and a primary procurement contact so we can send the 2-week agreement?

Thanks — I’ll loop Rishi and Aditya for technical follow-up.

—
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: petra_eval_pack_v1.zip (zip)
Attachment: petra_prompt_set_v1.csv (csv)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: PetraHealth model fit, eval pack, and pin/rollback options

Laura — quick technical note to surface to PetraHealth and to record internally.

Background: On Jan 12 we completed the staggered rollout of the compute-backed model stack (labelled redwood-2.0). During post-rollout validation we flagged a small but measurable change on clinical QA and guideline-grounded summarization. Key numbers from our internal A/B on a 2k-sample clinical prompt set (not identical to Petra’s eval pack but indicative):
- Overall accuracy proxy (task-specific metric): down 3.2% (p < 0.01)
- Hallucination incidence (our internal detector): 1.1% -> 3.8%
- Latency p50 improved ~9ms (expected)

Options for PetraHealth: 
A) Immediate pin to redwood-1.6-stable for the trial (no service interruption, customer-level model binding).
B) Continue on latest model but run the eval pack; if regressions show up, initiate a rollback on request (rollback takes ~2-4 hours to propagate for dedicated pools).
C) For Dedicated/Private customers we can create a private model slice pinned to an explicit build (requires a short setup).

I recommend A for a low-risk start. If Petra agrees, we should prepare:
- a minimal eval subset (5 prompts) to run within 24 hours and share quick diffs (I generated a sample diff attached).
- a short note for SRE to hold any automatic canary promotions for the Petra account during the trial window.

Attachment: regression_diff_sample.txt (diff snippet)

—
Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 17 Jan 2026 09:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: PetraHealth model fit, eval pack, and pin/rollback options

Thanks Aditya — I’ll propose option A to PetraHealth (pin to redwood-1.6-stable). Rishi, can you confirm the timeline & ops steps to request a customer-level pin for a 2-week trial? Specifically we need:
- Estimated time to enact pin (customer-level config change)
- Any SLO changes they should expect (latency/cost)
- Confirmation that automatic canary promotions will be blocked for the account during the trial window

I’ll reply to Emma with the trial start date options (Mon 1/26 or Mon 2/2) and ask procurement for quick PO details. I’ve attached a small diff sample Aditya produced so Petra can see a concrete example of the regression pattern.

Laura

Subject: Re: Post-demo: PetraHealth model fit, eval pack, and pin/rollback options

Laura — thanks for the detailed recap and for sharing the eval pack. A few quick responses from our side: 

1) Trial window: We like the idea of a conservative start. Tentatively target Mon 1/26 for a 2-week pinned trial to redwood-1.6-stable.
2) Procurement: procurement@petrahealth.com is copied; they’ll need the 2-week agreement and estimated cost.
3) Technical ask: Can you confirm the SLO impact (if any) when pinned to 1.6-stable vs 2.0? Also, we’d like explicit wording that automatic canary promotions will be blocked during our trial window.
4) Quick call: Could we do a 30-min call on Tue 1/20 at 11am ET to finalize the trial start & procurement items?

If you need anything from our side to run the initial 5-prompt subset, let us know and we’ll prioritize.

—
Emma Johnson
Senior Product Manager, PetraHealth
emma.johnson@petrahealth.com
